lines.en: What distinguishes a strong argument from a loud one is the quality of its evidence, not its volume.
It is a common mistake to attack the person instead of the argument, and it usually reveals a weak position.
Were the opposition's claims examined carefully, most of them would collapse under their own weight.
Admittedly, your plan has its strengths; nevertheless, it ignores the single most important risk.
Not until both sides agree on the facts can any real debate about solutions begin.
However appealing a slogan may sound, it is no substitute for a well-reasoned policy.
It is worth asking who benefits when a simple question is turned into a bitter public battle.
The strongest case for the proposal, granted, is its simplicity; its weakest is everything else.
To claim that technology alone will solve the problem is to misunderstand what the problem is.
Rarely does anyone win a debate by shouting; more often, they simply lose the audience.
What weakens his position is not the lack of passion, but the habit of treating every question as a personal attack.
It is perfectly possible to disagree with an idea while respecting the person who holds it, though you would never know it from our talk shows.
For the sake of argument, let us accept your claim; even then, your conclusion does not follow.
An argument won by silencing the other side is not a victory but a confession of weakness.
Were every debater required to state their opponent's position fairly before attacking it, half our arguments would end before they began.
